q-250404.name: Question 1
q-250404.problem: The inverse of the function $f(x)={e}^{2-x}$ is ${f}^{-1}(x)=${{field-1}}.
q-250404.worked_solution:
To find ${f}^{-1}(x),$ we start by replacing $f(x)$ with $y:$

$$
\begin{aligned}y & ={e}^{2-x}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, interchanging $x$ and $y$ gives

$$
\begin{aligned}x & ={e}^{2-y}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we make $y$ the subject of the equation as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}x & ={e}^{2-y} \\ \operatorname{ln}⁡x & =\operatorname{ln}⁡({e}^{2-y}) \\ \operatorname{ln}⁡x & =2-y \\ y & =2-\operatorname{ln}⁡x\end{aligned}
$$

    

Therefore, the inverse function is ${f}^{-1}(x)=2-\operatorname{ln}⁡x.$

q-148278.name: Question 2
q-148278.problem: The function $f(x)={e}^{x+k}+3$ has an inverse function given by ${f}^{-1}(x)=\operatorname{ln}⁡(x-3)+5.$ What is the value of $k?$
q-148278.worked_solution:
To find ${f}^{-1}(x),$ we start by replacing $f(x)$ with $y:$

$$
\begin{aligned}y & ={e}^{x+k}+3\end{aligned}
$$

Now, interchanging $x$ and $y$ gives

$$
\begin{aligned}x & ={e}^{y+k}+3.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we make $y$ the subject of the equation, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}x & ={e}^{y+k}+3 \\ {e}^{y+k} & =x-3 \\ \operatorname{ln}⁡({e}^{y+k}) & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(x-3) \\ y+k & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(x-3) \\ y & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(x-3)-k\end{aligned}
$$

    

Therefore, the inverse function is ${f}^{-1}(x)=\operatorname{ln}⁡(x-3)-k.$

Comparing our answer with the given expression, we conclude that $k=-5.$

q-148313.name: Question 3
q-148313.problem: Find the inverse of the function $f(x)={7}^{x-2}+4.$
q-148313.worked_solution:
To find ${f}^{-1}(x),$ we start by replacing $f(x)$ with $y:$

$$
\begin{aligned}y & ={7}^{x-2}+4\end{aligned}
$$

Now, interchanging $x$ and $y$ gives

$$
\begin{aligned}x & ={7}^{y-2}+4.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we make $y$ the subject of the equation, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}x & ={7}^{y-2}+4 \\ x-4 & ={7}^{y-2} \\ {log}_{7}⁡(x-4) & ={log}_{7}⁡({7}^{y-2}) \\ {log}_{7}⁡(x-4) & =y-2 \\ y & ={log}_{7}⁡(x-4)+2\end{aligned}
$$

    

Therefore, the inverse function is ${f}^{-1}(x)={log}_{7}⁡(x-4)+2.$

$$

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =\frac{2}{5}\cdot {3}^{ky}+2\end{aligned}

$$

Find the inverse of the function f(x)=14⋅32x−12.

a
f−1(x)=2log3⁡(x+12)
b
f−1(x)=12log3⁡(4x+2)
c
f−1(x)=2log3⁡(4x+12)
d

e
f−1(x)=log3⁡(x+12)+2
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

To find f−1(x), we start by replacing f(x) with y:

y=14⋅32x−12

Now, interchanging x and y gives x=14⋅32y−12.

Finally, we make y the subject of the equation, as follows:

x=14⋅32y−1214⋅32y=x+1232y=4x+2log3⁡(32y)=log3⁡(4x+2)2y=log3⁡(4x+2)y=12log3⁡(4x+2)

Therefore, the inverse function is f−1(x)=12log3⁡(4x+2).

q-148349.name: Question 9
q-148349.problem: Find the inverse of the function $f(x)=\frac{1}{2}\cdot {e}^{x+1}-2.$
q-148349.worked_solution:
To find ${f}^{-1}(x),$ we start by replacing $f(x)$ with $y:$

$$
\begin{aligned}y & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot {e}^{x+1}-2\end{aligned}
$$

Now, interchanging $x$ and $y$ gives

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot {e}^{y+1}-2.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we make $y$ the subject of the equation, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot {e}^{y+1}-2 \\ \frac{1}{2}\cdot {e}^{y+1} & =x+2 \\ {e}^{y+1} & =2x+4 \\ \operatorname{ln}⁡({e}^{y+1}) & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(2x+4) \\ y+1 & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(2x+4) \\ y & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(2x+4)-1\end{aligned}
$$

    

Therefore, the inverse function is ${f}^{-1}(x)=\operatorname{ln}⁡(2x+4)-1.$

q-148367.problem:
The function $f(x)=\frac{2}{3}-{5}^{2x-k}$ has an inverse function given by 

$$
{f}^{-1}(x)=\frac{1}{2}{log}_{5}⁡(\frac{2-3x}{3}).
$$

What is the value of $k?$
q-148367.worked_solution:
To find ${f}^{-1}(x),$ we start by replacing $f(x)$ with $y:$

$$
\begin{aligned}y & =\frac{2}{3}-{5}^{2x-k}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, interchanging $x$ and $y$ gives

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =\frac{2}{3}-{5}^{2y-k}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we make $y$ the subject of the equation, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =\frac{2}{3}-{5}^{2y-k} \\ {5}^{2y-k} & =\frac{2}{3}-x \\ {5}^{2y-k} & =\frac{2-3x}{3} \\ {log}_{5}⁡({5}^{2y-k}) & ={log}_{5}⁡(\frac{2-3x}{3}) \\ 2y-k & ={log}_{5}⁡(\frac{2-3x}{3}) \\ 2y & ={log}_{5}⁡(\frac{2-3x}{3})+k \\ y & =\frac{1}{2}{log}_{5}⁡(\frac{2-3x}{3})+\frac{k}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

    

Therefore, the inverse function is ${f}^{-1}(x)=\frac{1}{2}{log}_{5}⁡(\frac{2-3x}{3})+\frac{k}{2}$  

Comparing our answer with the given expression, we conclude that $k=0.$

q-250483.problem: The inverse of the function $f(x)=\frac{1}{2}{log}_{2}⁡(x)+\frac{1}{2}$ is ${f}^{-1}(x)=${{field-1}}.

$$
\begin{aligned}y & =\frac{1}{2}{log}_{2}⁡(x)+\frac{1}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, interchanging $x$ and $y$ gives

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =\frac{1}{2}{log}_{2}⁡(y)+\frac{1}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we make $y$ the subject of the equation, as follows:        

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =\frac{1}{2}{log}_{2}⁡(y)+\frac{1}{2} \\ x-\frac{1}{2} & =\frac{1}{2}{log}_{2}⁡y \\ 2x-1 & ={log}_{2}⁡y \\ {2}^{2x-1} & ={2}^{{log}_{2}⁡y} \\ {2}^{2x-1} & =y \\ y & ={2}^{2x-1}\end{aligned}
$$

q-46621.problem: Find the inverse of the function $f(x)=\operatorname{log}⁡(\frac{x}{3}).$
q-46621.worked_solution:
To find ${f}^{-1}(x),$ we start by replacing $f(x)$ with $y:$

$$
\begin{aligned}y & =\operatorname{log}⁡(\frac{x}{3})\end{aligned}
$$

Now, interchanging $x$ and $y$ gives

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =\operatorname{log}⁡(\frac{y}{3}).\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we make $y$ the subject of the equation, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =\operatorname{log}⁡(\frac{y}{3}) \\ {10}^{x} & ={10}^{\operatorname{log}⁡(y/3)} \\ {10}^{x} & =\frac{y}{3} \\ y & =3\cdot {10}^{x}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the inverse function is ${f}^{-1}(x)=3\cdot {10}^{x}.$

q-46629.problem: Find the inverse of the function $f(x)=\operatorname{ln}⁡(7x).$
q-46629.worked_solution:
To find ${f}^{-1}(x),$ we start by replacing $f(x)$ with $y:$

$$
\begin{aligned}y & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(7x)\end{aligned}
$$

Now, interchanging $x$ and $y$ gives

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(7y).\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(7y) \\ {e}^{x} & ={e}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡(7y)} \\ {e}^{x} & =7y \\ y & =\frac{{e}^{x}}{7}\end{aligned}

Comparing our answer with the given expression, we conclude that $k=-9.$

$$

$$

Finally, we make $y$ the subject of the equation, as follows:

$$
